[2026-11-25] c:7161926998 comment by fanquake (member):
[quoted text omitted]

I'm not really convinced about backporting these (release infrastructure) changes at this point, especially since nobody else has complained / noticed that the native RISC-V build isn't working, in the month since `32.1` was released. I also think if we want this to work reliably, we should at least have a (weekly? given the low resources of boards) smoke test or similar, of the build.
[2026-11-25] c:7163594130 comment by hebasto (member):
[quoted text omitted]

That's expected, because RISC-V release binaries are available on the website and there are no issues with building Bitcoin Core from source natively on RISC-V.

For recent releases, we had a very nice property: reproducibility across build platforms, including `x86_64`, `arm64` and `riscv64`. This property became weaker in the 32.x release branch, and I do believe it's worth restoring.

[quoted text omitted]
I agree. I'll think about that.
[2026-11-25] c:7164022560 comment by fanquake (member):
[quoted text omitted]

Not sure what you mean. I'm talking about doing Guix builds on RISC-V, which doesn't currently work for `32.x`. The fact that nobody else has complained/noticed, probably points to nobody else doing, or relying on these builds.

[quoted text omitted]
Sure, and it has been restored in master. However this was known to be broken for ~6 months before `32.x` was to be branched off (see discussion in #34550), and not fixed (until it was too late), and then those fixes broke other things (hence the additional changes here). I think going forward, what is needed is more (timely) testing of builds that are considered important, rather than changing release branches after the fact.
